answer: A durable defense is stake-bonded reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and peers score its work over time. Crossing the ridge of accumulated trust takes weeks of useful service, not a whisper of a fresh keypair, so spawning thousands of fake identities no longer buys influence. Each pearl of reputation must be earned and can be slashed for fraud. An attacker wanting 1,000 trusted voices must fund 1,000 deposits and sustain 1,000 histories, turning a cheap identity flood into a costly, slow and easily detected investment.
